page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-48 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1410.49 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 23.8 GB/sec. However, the 48 vCPUs deliver average multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 44617.16 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10859.0. Memory bandwidth is solid, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 2446.02 GB/sec and uncached large block writes at 79.98 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AES cryptography, which assist in tasks like Passmark CPU encryption and software compilation.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-highcpu-48 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio. With only 1 GB of RAM per vCPU, it is not configured for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data caching. However, for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, this configuration offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency by avoiding the expense of unneeded RAM. It is well-suited for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and moderate-scale multi-threaded decompression.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-48 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 48 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It contains 24 physical cores with hyper-threading, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks reveal average multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10859.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 44617.16, contrasted by weaker single-core performance. With a 1:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, it is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, memory-light tasks. It is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and multi-threaded processing.
